messages:
alex.cheung: quick heads-up, perf spike after the kernel-selector tweak on canary. Host CPU for preparse jumped ~35% on p95. Flamegraph points at parse_token_stream and http2-fragment-handler.
zoe: ugh. timeline? which commit? :eyes: 
alex.cheung: rolled 2026-03-18 03:14 UTC - commit 0b3f2a kernel selector change (prefer fused-attn for small seqs). perf snippet:
```
# perf top -p pid
 22.4% parse_token_stream
 18.1% http2_fragment_handler
 12.3% kv_cache_lookup
 6.5% memcpy
```
matt: interesting that kv_cache_lookup is nontrivial. can you paste a flamegraph link? anya: maybe fragmentation increases kvcache churn; small fused-attn lowers GPU time so host work becomes dominant.
alex.cheung: flame link https://perf.redwood/fg/327890 - shows hotspots in parse->chunk_coalesce->kv_index_resolve. also saw many small gRPC frames: average payload ~430B, >1k calls/s
zoe: small frames = more syscall overhead. did we change streaming chunking heuristics?
matt: yes, we bumped chunk boundary sensitivity to reduce latency on long seqs. side effect: short requests stop coalescing.
anya: hypothesis: kernel change reduced model compute per-token; host now needs better batching heuristics to keep throughput. we should try two experiments:
1) re-enable adaptive coalesce for frames <1KB (tweak: ingress.coalesce.min_batch_bytes=1024)
2) introduce kv-score to prefer keeping hot keys in memory longer (kv.eviction.bias=hotness*1.2)
alex.cheung: ran experiment 1 on canary; p95 CPU dropped 18%, but tail latency for single-token chat increased 4ms. logs:
```
[ingress] coalesce: merged 73% of short frames
[host] p95 cpu per req: 48ms -> 39ms
[gRPC] number of writev calls: 1.2M -> 0.6M
```
zoe: nice. can we get a throughput vs latency curve? matt: attaching quick numbers from 5k qps ephemeral run: baseline p50=25ms p95=120ms; experiment1 p50=27ms p95=99ms; tokens/sec +6%
anya: experiment2 (kv bias) on different canary reduced kvcache misses by 9% but memory stayed within limits. combined both = best of both worlds.
infra-bot: deploy canary-flag: ingress.coalesce.min_batch_bytes=1024 rolled to awsdedicated-2
alex.cheung: next steps: 1) prod rolling with coalesce flag off by default for small-tier hosts 2) add kernel-selector telemetry to measure host:gpu ratio per request 3) add regression test in perf CI (simulate high short-request mix)
zoe: also add a guard: if host cpu >65% on node then fallback to less aggressive coalesce to keep tail down.
matt: created PR #1247 for the adaptive coalesce toggle
anya: will run 24h canary for combined flags and gather flamegraphs at 1h intervals
alex.cheung: thanks team. logging saved in /var/logs/perf/327890/ - ping me if you need traces :thumbsup:
zoe: :party-parrot:
